title: Ledger wallet tampering suspected after crypto thefts linked to CryptoBillis hardware
content:
Ledger has warned that users of its cryptocurrency hardware wallet have experienced account drainings that appear linked to tampered devices sold by the reseller CryptoBillis. The company has asked CryptoBillis to halt all sales of Ledger wallets while an investigation proceeds.

Ledger confirmed that “one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant.” Images posted on X and Threads show a small circuit board positioned beneath the screen, which the company says can intercept anything displayed, including the seed passphrase shown during initial setup, and can transmit data via an embedded SIM card.
summary: Users of Ledger crypto wallets have reported account drains that appear tied to tampered hardware sold by CryptoBillis. Ledger has asked CryptoBillis to pause all wallet sales while it investigates a confirmed unauthorized hardware implant—a small circuit board under the screen that can intercept the seed passphrase using an embedded SIM card.
author: The Verge

title: DistroKid removes songs after UMG lawsuit alleging AI‑slop pipeline
content:
DistroKid has been removing songs from its platform in direct response to a lawsuit filed by Universal Music Group (UMG). The company confirmed to The Verge that the takedowns are a reaction to claims made by UMG, which sued in September alleging that DistroKid has created an “AI‑slop pipeline.”  

Artists have taken to social media to complain that their work was removed without any notice. Musician McGwire, who describes himself as a “Video Game boy,” said six of his songs were taken down from streaming services and that DistroKid provided no communication before or after the removals. The situation has sparked concerns among independent musicians about the impact of the lawsuit‑driven purge.
summary: DistroKid confirmed it is taking down songs in response to a lawsuit filed by UMG that claims the service created an “AI‑slop pipeline.” Artists, including musician McGwire who lost six songs, say the removals happened without any notice from DistroKid.
author: The Verge

title: Petra Power aims to modernize energy for data centers and defense vehicles
content:
Petra Power, a startup, is targeting the modernization of energy supplies for data centers and defense vehicles.  

The company says its fuel‑cell technology is “super efficient” and can cut fuel costs, a claim it makes as the tech industry faces a shortage of electricity.  

Petra Power asserts that its solution addresses the current demand‑supply gap for power‑intensive operations.
summary: Petra Power says its fuel cells are super efficient and cut fuel costs. The startup is targeting data centers and defense vehicles amid a tech industry electricity shortage.
author: TechCrunch

title: King warns malicious online actors evolving tactics in NCSC 10th anniversary letter
content: The King warned that malicious online actors are evolving tactics in a letter issued to mark the 10th anniversary of the National Cyber Security Centre. In the letter, he spoke of “threats to our international order.” The communication coincides with the centre’s decade‑long milestone.
summary: The King said malicious online actors are evolving their tactics. He made the remarks in a letter marking the 10th anniversary of the National Cyber Security Centre, calling them threats to the international order.
author: BBC Technology

title: Evacuations and injuries reported after alleged Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
content:
Evacuations and injuries were reported at Riyadh’s international airport following another alleged Houthi attack, officials said.  

The incident comes just two days after three Saudi citizens were killed in Houthi‑claimed attacks on the same airport on Thursday.  

Authorities noted the latest strike prompted the airport’s evacuation and resulted in injuries among those present.
summary: Evacuations and injuries were reported at Riyadh's international airport following an alleged Houthi attack. The incident comes two days after three Saudi citizens were killed in Houthi-claimed attacks on the same airport on Thursday.
author: Euronews

title: Mahmoud Abbas postpones legislative elections, schedules presidential vote for Sep 11 2027
content:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas announced on Saturday that the legislative elections, originally scheduled for next month, will be postponed until September 11, 2027. He also called for a presidential poll on the same date. Abbas cited Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories as the reasons for the delay.

The decision was reported by our correspondent in Jerusalem, Noga Tarnopolsky.
summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas postponed the legislative elections that were due next month until September 11, 2027. He also called for a presidential poll on the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
author: France 24

title: Kenya reports negative Ebola test for suspected patient as contact tracing proceeds
content:
Kenya: Ebola tests negative as contact tracing continues

Tests have come back negative for a person suspected of having Ebola who was reportedly in quarantine at a hospital, following rumours circulating over the past 24 hours.  

Meanwhile, in Nairobi, authorities are racing to trace contacts of Kenya's first Ebola death, reported on Monday.  

Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.
summary: Tests have come back negative for a person suspected of having Ebola who was in quarantine at a hospital. Authorities in Nairobi are racing to trace contacts of Kenya's first Ebola death reported on Monday.
author: France 24

title: Durban police confront second day of anti‑migrant unrest, looting and arson
content:
South Africa: Anti‑migrant unrest flares in Durban

Police in Durban were battling a fresh wave of anti‑migrant unrest. Shops were looted, homes were torched and foreign nationals were targeted as crowds took to the streets for a second day.

The violence has revived fears of rising xenophobic tensions over immigration.
summary: Police in Durban were battling a fresh wave of anti‑migrant unrest that saw crowds take to the streets for a second day. The unrest involved looting of shops, torching of homes and targeting of foreign nationals, reviving fears of rising xenophobic tensions over immigration.
author: France 24

title: Indian police detain head of satirical Cockroach Party before Election Commission protest
content:
Indian police detained the head of the satirical “cockroach” online movement on Saturday. The arrest came just before a major protest against the Election Commission, which prompted strict security measures.

France 24’s Andrew Hilliar noted that the authorities “seem to have seen that coming.” In a prerecorded video, Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Party, announced an interim leader to take over the group.
summary: Indian police detained the head of the satirical “cockroach” online movement on Saturday, the group said, ahead of a major protest against the Election Commission that prompted strict security measures. In a prerecorded video, Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Party, named an interim leader to take over.
author: France 24

title: Christa Pike discharged from hospital, returned to prison after botched execution
content:
Christa Pike, a 50‑year‑old convicted murderer, was discharged from the hospital and returned to prison after a botched execution attempt.  

Pike’s lawyers announced on Saturday that she had been released from the hospital and sent back to prison. She had been transported to the hospital in critical condition on September 30, after surviving Tennessee’s failed execution attempt for the murder of a classmate when she was a teenager.
summary: Lawyers said on Saturday that the 50-year-old convicted murderer Christa Pike has been discharged from the hospital and returned to prison. She was transported to the hospital in critical condition on September 30 after she survived Tennessee's botched effort to execute her for murdering a classmate when she was a teenager.
author: France 24

title: Riyadh airport suspends operations after Houthi attack wounds multiple people
content:
Saudi authorities announced on Saturday that operations at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport had been suspended after a new attack left multiple people wounded.

The airport had already suffered an attack by the Houthis on Thursday, which killed three people and damaged a plane. The Iran‑backed group did not announce any new attacks on Saturday.

The airport remains closed following the latest incident.
summary: Saudi authorities suspended operations at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport after a new attack left multiple people wounded. The Houthi attack on Thursday killed three people and damaged a plane, but the group did not announce any new attacks on Saturday.
author: France 24

title: Women remain underrepresented in US politics ahead of November 3 midterm elections
content:
The United States is preparing for midterm elections on November 3, during which Congress and state governors will be elected.  

Women remain underrepresented at every level of U.S. politics. However, the upcoming midterms could bring historic victories for female candidates.  

The elections may therefore mark a significant moment for women seeking political office in the United States.
summary: The United States is holding elections for Congress and state governors. Women are underrepresented at all levels of US politics, but they may win historic victories in the midterms on November 3.
author: DW World

title: Thousands march in London, Berlin and Rome demanding end to Israel's war on Gaza
content: Thousands of protesters marched across Europe demanding an end to Israel’s war on Gaza, as shown in a series of photographs. Demonstrations were held in London, Berlin and Rome, where participants denounced ongoing Israeli attacks on Gaza. The rallies coincided with the anniversary of a ceasefire related to the conflict.
summary: Thousands marched in London, Berlin and Rome demanding an end to Israel's war on Gaza. The demonstrations denounced ongoing Israeli attacks on Gaza on the ceasefire anniversary.
author: Al Jazeera

title: More Israeli attacks kill Palestinians in Gaza one year after US‑brokered ceasefire
content: One year after a US‑brokered ceasefire was agreed, Palestinians continue to be killed in Gaza. Israeli attacks have persisted, resulting in further Palestinian fatalities despite the ceasefire’s anniversary. The ongoing violence underscores that the ceasefire has not halted hostilities in the enclave.
summary: More Israeli attacks have killed Palestinians in Gaza. This occurs one year after the US‑brokered ceasefire was agreed.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspended by Portugal FA after walkout and coach criticism
content: Portugal star Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation after walking out of the national team camp and criticizing the coach during Nations League matches. The federation’s disciplinary action follows the forward’s departure from the squad and public remarks aimed at the team’s manager. Ronaldo’s suspension was announced in response to the walkout, which occurred amid the Nations League games. The federation confirmed the penalty without providing further details.
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended by the Portuguese football association. The suspension follows his walkout from the national team camp and criticism of the coach during Nations League games.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump says Ukraine needs new president who will agree to end war
content:
Former President Donald Trump said Ukraine needs a new president who will agree to end the war, adding that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to bring the conflict to a close.  

Trump made the remarks while tensions between the United States and Kyiv have risen over a diesel deal between Ukraine and Russia.  

The comments reflect ongoing disagreements between Trump and the Ukrainian leadership regarding the war and related energy arrangements.
summary: Trump said Ukraine needs a new president who will agree to end the war. He suggested Zelenskyy has not done enough to end the war amid tensions with Kyiv over a diesel deal with Russia.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Expedition seeks Amelia Earhart's plane on remote island
content:
An expedition is heading to a remote island in the hope of locating aviator Amelia Earhart’s missing plane. The team’s goal is to solve the long‑standing mystery surrounding her 1937 disappearance.  

The group is currently en route to the suspected crash site, aiming to uncover evidence that could finally explain what happened to Earhart in 1937.
summary: An expedition is traveling to a remote island believed to be the suspected crash site of aviator Amelia Earhart. The team hopes to locate her plane and solve the mystery of her 1937 disappearance.
author: BBC World

title: Trump says Ukraine needs new president after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
content:
Former President Donald Trump said it is “time for Ukraine to get a new president” after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned a proposed diesel deal with Russia. Zelensky argued that the arrangement, which would see Russian diesel released into the United States, would enable Moscow to fund its war.

The Ukrainian leader’s criticism links the diesel shipment directly to financial support for Russia’s military operations. Trump’s call for a leadership change follows Zelensky’s warning about the potential impact of the deal.
summary: Trump said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president. Zelensky said a diesel deal with Russia to release diesel into the United States would help Moscow fund the war.
author: BBC World

title: Darkness Falls could become first Triple Crown winner since Nijinsky after Dewhurst win
content:
Darkness Falls has reignited hopes of becoming the first horse to win the Triple Crown since Nijinsky in 1970 following a narrow victory in the Dewhurst Stakes. The race took place at York, where the field started with a level break before all horses moved to the far rail after two furlongs.

Hickory Lad held a narrow lead during the contest, with Love A Giggle also in contention. Cut A Dash made a charge down the middle of the track as the runners approached the finish line.
summary: Darkness Falls won the Dewhurst Stakes narrowly and could become the first Triple Crown winner since Nijinsky in 1970. In the Rockingham race at York, the field had a level break, all horses ended on the far rail after two furlongs, with Hickory Lad leading narrowly, Love A Giggle also, and Cut A Dash charging home down the middle.
author: Guardian Sport

title: UN condemns racist abuse of Coco Gauff, warns Black female athletes targeted
content:
The United Nations’ human rights office has condemned the racist abuse directed at American tennis player Coco Gauff, describing the online messages as “appalling and illustrate that Black female athletes are specifically targeted for vitriol and racial abuse.” The statement was issued by the office’s high commissioner, Volker Türk, in a social media post on Saturday.

In the post, the UN human rights office called for solidarity to help push back against racism and sexism. The organization specifically highlighted the targeting of Black female athletes, urging a collective response to the “appalling vitriol” faced by Gauff.
summary: The United Nations' human rights office condemned the racist online messages sent to American tennis player Coco Gauff. High Commissioner Volker Türk stated that the abuse illustrates that Black female athletes are specifically targeted for vitriol and racial abuse.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Paul Seixas becomes youngest winner of Giro di Lombardia
content:
Paul Seixas claimed a historic victory at the Giro di Lombardia, ending his breakout season with a stunning win at the Classic of the Falling Leaves. The 20‑year‑old French rider became the youngest winner of the race and the fourth‑youngest to win a Monument.

Seixas finished 48 seconds ahead of Vuelta champion Enric Mas, who took second place. Italian rider Giulio Ciccone rounded out the podium, finishing just over a minute behind Seixas.
summary: Paul Seixas, 20, won the Giro di Lombardia, becoming the youngest winner of the Classic of the Falling Leaves. Enric Mas finished second, 48 seconds behind, and Giulio Ciccone took third.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bruno Guimarães comeback ends Leeds unbeaten run for Arsenal
content:
Bruno Guimarães completed his Arsenal debut with a goal that ended Leeds United’s unbeaten run, turning the match around after the visitors took the lead. Leeds had dominated the first half and held a one-goal advantage when Arsenal managed to snatch an equalizer. Mikel Arteta subsequently introduced his key summer signing, the former Newcastle captain, just after the 60th minute to shift the momentum.

Guimarães immediately impacted the game, helping Arsenal play with greater intensity against the resilient Leeds side. His introduction proved decisive in overriding the opposition's hard-fought performance, allowing Arsenal to secure the victory and build on their competitive foundation.
summary: Arsenal ended Leeds' unbeaten run after Bruno Guimarães came off the bench to turn the game on its head. The former Newcastle captain entered the field just after the hour following an equalizer against a dominant Leeds side.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Verstappen secures Singapore GP pole ahead of Leclerc, Russell crashes in sprint
content:
Max Verstappen secured pole position for the Singapore Grand Prix, edging out Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in a close battle on the Marina Bay streets after the sprint race.  

Lewis Hamilton qualified third, while Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli finished fourth.  George Russell, who had been leading the sprint on lap one, crashed out and will start from the back of the grid on Sunday.
summary: Max Verstappen took pole position for the Singapore Grand Prix, beating Charles Leclerc into second place. George Russell crashed out of the sprint while leading on lap one, and Lewis Hamilton qualified third with Kimi Antonelli fourth for Mercedes.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lionesses beat Greece 3-1; Rayo Vallecano match suspended after fan disruption
content:
Live coverage of Saturday’s afternoon kick‑offs includes matches such as Chelsea v Bournemouth and Sunderland v Brighton, with updates on scores, tables and ten things to look out for.  

The England Lionesses won 3‑1 against Greece in the first leg of their World Cup qualifying play‑off, and Suzy Wrack provided an analysis of the performance.  

In La Liga, a match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Bilbao was suspended after Rayo Vallecano supporters threw paper airplanes and other objects onto the field. The match was suspended.
summary: The Lionesses defeated Greece 3-1 in the first leg of their World Cup qualifying play‑off. Rayo Vallecano supporters disrupted their La Liga match against Athletic Bilbao by throwing paper airplanes and other objects, forcing the game to be suspended.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Verstappen beats Ferraris to Singapore pole
content:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen secured pole position in qualifying for the Singapore Grand Prix, outpacing the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton.

Verstappen’s fastest lap earned him the front‑row spot on the grid, while Leclerc and Hamilton finished behind him in the Ferrari cars.
summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen secured pole position in qualifying at the Singapore Grand Prix. He beat the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump skips Alabama game for Tennessee rally; debate continues over Hasan execution livestream
content: President Trump confirmed on Friday that he would not attend the University of Georgia versus University of Alabama football game in Tuscaloosa due to Hurricane Isaias. Despite canceling his plans for the game, the President stated he would still travel to Tennessee for a midterm rally, describing it as a "Big Rally" that was quickly organized.
summary: President Trump confirmed he will not attend the University of Georgia vs. University of Alabama football game due to Hurricane Isaias. He stated that he will instead travel to Tennessee for a midterm rally while a debate continues over the livestream of Hasan's execution.
author: The Hill

title: Democratic lawmakers protest Trump's lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel
content: Democratic lawmakers criticized President Trump’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian oil, citing ongoing global fuel shortages driven by U.S. military operations against Iran and the Russia-Ukraine war. The move allows Russian President Vladimir Putin’s government to supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the United States and the global marketplace.
summary: Democratic lawmakers pushed back Friday on President Trump's decision to lift sanctions on Russian oil amid global fuel shortages during U.S. military operations against Iran and the Russia-Ukraine war. The deal will allow Russian President Vladimir Putin’s government to supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the U.S. and the global marketplace.
author: The Hill

title: Kalshi Investigates Suspicious Bets on Trump Press Secretary Appointment
content: Prediction market Kalshi has launched an investigation into suspicious betting activity connected to President Trump’s choice for his next press secretary, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. The company stated that it is examining at least three trades executed on its platform shortly before news outlets started announcing the appointment of Katie Zacharia to the White House.
summary: Prediction market Kalshi has opened an investigation into suspicious bets related to President Trump’s selection of his next press secretary. The company said that it was looking into at least three trades placed on its platform shortly before news outlets announced the appointment of Katie Zacharia.
author: The Hill

title: Talarico makes first appearance in 13 days at ACL music festival after flu absence
content:
Texas Senate candidate James Talarico (D) made his first public appearance in nearly two weeks on Friday, marking a return after a thirteen-day absence. His campaign previously announced that the Democratic nominee was recovering from a bout of the flu.

Talarico was spotted strolling through the Austin City Limits (ACL), an annual music festival held in Texas’s capital city. Videos documenting his presence at the event have been shared on social media.
summary: Texas Senate candidate James Talarico made his first appearance in nearly two weeks on Friday after recovering from the flu. The Democratic nominee was seen at the Austin City Limits music festival in Texas's capital city.
author: The Hill

title: Hegseth's military execution livestream and Guilfoyle scandal draw bipartisan criticism
content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faced bipartisan criticism over plans to livestream a military execution. The proposed move drew significant political backlash from members of both parties.

Separately, US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle is involved in a scandal. The controversy centers on her role as the ambassador to Greece.
summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces bipartisan blowback over plans to livestream a military execution. A scandal involving US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle is also highlighted in the political news.
author: NPR Politics

title: South African billionaire Koos Bekker turns Somerset estate into luxury hotel
content:
South African billionaire Koos Bekker has transformed a former country estate in Somerset into the Newt estate, a development that includes luxury hotels, pubs, and high street businesses. Local residents initially viewed his purchase of the old estate as a positive sign for the area’s improvement.

The estate features peaceful, manicured gardens characterized by a maze of apple trees twisted into perfect shapes using the espalier method. Despite the picturesque setting, local concerns persist regarding issues such as flooding.
summary: Koos Bekker’s Newt estate encompasses luxury hotels, pubs and high street business, with local concerns including floodingWhen South African billionaire Koos Bekker bought an old country estate in a sleepy corner of Somerset to turn it into a luxury hotel, residents thought it was a sign their area was on the up. Walking through his peaceful manicured gardens, which feature a maze of apple trees twisted into perfect shapes using the espalier method, it’s easy to feel that all is well in this quiet, picturesque pocket of England.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Colorado Anschutz study shows horseback riding reduces hyperactivity in autistic children.
content: New research from the University of Colorado Anschutz indicates that horseback riding can help reduce hyperactivity in children with autism and other psychiatric disorders. The study provides strong evidence that this horse-based activity improves various behavioral and emotional challenges in these youth.
summary: New research from the University of Colorado Anschutz shows that horseback riding can reduce hyperactivity in children with autism. The study also indicates that horseback riding improves other behavioral and emotional challenges
author: Medical Xpress

title: Physical activity weakens genetic risk link to depression severity, long‑term data show
content:
Physical activity weakens link between genetic risk and depression severity, long‑term data suggest.

Major depressive disorder (MDD), one type of depression, is one of the most common psychiatric conditions worldwide. It is characterized by persistent low mood and a loss of interest in everyday activities, along with changes in sleep, appetite and motivation.
summary: Physical activity weakens the link between genetic risk and depression severity, according to long‑term data. Major depressive disorder is characterized by persistent low mood, loss of interest, and changes in sleep, appetite, and motivation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New genetic candidates may explain male predominance in autism
content:
Researchers at Baylor College of Medicine, the Duncan Neurological Research Institute (Duncan NRI) at Texas Children’s Hospital, and collaborating institutions have identified new genetic candidates that may explain why autism is diagnosed about four times more often in boys than in girls.

The study, published in the American Journal of Human Genetics, reveals that small changes in the gene MECP2 on the X chromosome might help explain part of this difference.
summary: Researchers at Baylor College of Medicine, the Duncan Neurological Research Institute (Duncan NRI) at Texas Children's Hospital, and collaborating institutions identified new genetic candidates that may explain why autism is diagnosed about four times more often in boys than in girls. The study, published in the American Journal of Human Genetics, shows that small changes in the gene MECP2 on the X chromosome might account for part of this difference.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Future medicine using mechanical cell memory could erase crow's feet and laugh lines.
content:
The medicine of the future could be driven by mechanical cell memory. According to the source, this approach is not a cure for baldness, but it may eliminate crow's feet and laugh lines by instructing the tissues in the face to remember their more elastic youth.

The concept suggests that facial tissues could be guided to regain youthful elasticity, though no additional details are provided.
summary: It is not a cure for baldness. It might eliminate crow's feet and laugh lines by telling facial tissues to remember their more elastic youth.
author: Medical Xpress

title: A healthy Nordic diet may help you to live longer, but liver benefits remain unclear
content:
A healthy Nordic diet may help you to live longer, but liver benefits remain unclear.  

The Nordic diet, described as a northern version of the Mediterranean diet, is a healthy, sustainable way of eating based on traditional foods from Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland. It includes plant foods and berries, whole grains, low‑fat dairy products and fatty fish.  

In general, people who eat a healthy diet give themselves a significantly better chance of avoiding some major diseases than those who don't.
summary: In general, people who eat a healthy diet give themselves a significantly better chance of avoiding some major diseases than those who don't. The Nordic diet, also known as a northern version of the Mediterranean diet, is a healthy, sustainable way of eating based on traditional foods of countries like Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Radiation Exposure Linked to Pulmonary Hypertension in Lung Cancer Patients
content:
Radiation exposure linked to pulmonary hypertension after lung cancer treatment

Lung cancer patients undergoing radiation treatment may be at higher risk of developing pulmonary hypertension, a type of high blood pressure that affects the arteries that carry blood from the right side of the heart to the lungs.

Pulmonary hypertension can increase pressure in these arteries over time. The sustained high pressure may eventually lead to right‑sided heart failure.
summary: Lung cancer patients undergoing radiation treatment may be at higher risk of developing pulmonary hypertension. The increased pressure can eventually lead to right-sided heart failure.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Wealth gaps linked to 15-year life expectancy gap in Norway, U.S.; WHO warns targets missed
content:
A recent World Health Organization report highlights that socioeconomic circumstances influence life expectancy, noting that poorer people, on average, live shorter lives. This pattern is evident even in wealthy countries with extensive welfare systems.

In Norway, for instance, 40‑year‑old men in the richest 1% could expect to live almost 14 years longer than those in the poorest 1%. In the United States, the equivalent gap is nearly 15 years.

The report warns that international targets for reducing health inequalities by 2040 are likely to be missed.
summary: Poorer people, on average, live shorter lives. This pattern can be seen even in wealthy countries with extensive welfare systems.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Retailers such as BJ’s and Lululemon trim assortments to spur growth
content:
Retailers such as BJ’s and Lululemon are cutting back on product assortments as a strategy to improve performance.  

Retail brands are shrinking their assortments to return to healthy growth, while box stores are culling products to better curate their offerings and stabilize their businesses.
summary: Retail brands are shrinking their product assortments to return to healthy growth. Box stores are culling items to better curate selections and stabilize their businesses.
author: CNBC Business

title: Flock Safety to cut 270 jobs amid backlash over AI surveillance
content:
Flock Safety, a surveillance technology startup known for its AI-powered cameras and license-plate readers, plans to cut approximately 18% of its workforce, according to people with direct knowledge of the plans. The layoffs are expected to impact roughly 270 employees and will take effect at the end of the month.

The job reductions come after a voluntary buyout program and occur as the company faces increasing opposition from communities and lawmakers. Flock, which has experienced rapid growth in recent years, has been under scrutiny due to growing privacy concerns regarding its products.
summary: Flock Safety plans to eliminate roughly 270 positions, about 18% of its workforce, after a voluntary buyout program. The layoffs will take effect at the end of the month as the company faces mounting opposition from communities and lawmakers over its AI-powered surveillance cameras and license‑plate readers.
author: Guardian Business

title: UAW President Shawn Fain wins re-election, defeating challenger Rich Boyer
content:
Shawn Fain, the president of the United Auto Workers, has secured a decisive re-election victory over challenger Rich Boyer, who received only 13% of the vote. The election, which determines leadership for a four-year term, was marked by a campaign period complicated by accusations of corruption and election interference that dogged Fain.

The union’s voting process initiated with the distribution of mail-in ballots in late August 2026, and vote tabulating began on October 6.
summary: Shawn Fain easily won re-election as president of the United Auto Workers despite a campaign marred by accusations of corruption and election interference. Challenger Rich Boyer received just 13% of the vote in the election for a four-year term.
author: Guardian Business

title: ‘People are pissed’: union decries TSA’s removal of chairs for checkpoint staff
content:
The American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE) has criticized the Transportation Security Administration’s decision to remove all chairs from airport checkpoints, citing a drop in staff morale. The order for TSA workers to remain standing is said to “reinforce professionalism,” but union officials argue it is detrimental to employee well‑being.

AFGE officials have launched a campaign to restore seating for TSA staff. Johnny Jones, secretary‑treasurer of AFGE TSA council 100 and president of AFGE local 1040, which represents TSA workers in Dallas‑Fort Worth, said, “People are pissed.” The chairs were removed by the Trump administration unilaterally.

The union’s campaign seeks to allow airport security staff to sit once more at checkpoints.
summary: Order for workers to remain standing to ‘reinforce professionalism’ draws rebuke amid plunging moraleUnion officials have launched a campaign to allow airport security staff to sit once more after the Trump administration unilaterally removed all the chairs for Transportation Security Administration (TSA) staff at checkpoints.“People are pissed,” said Johnny Jones, secretary-treasurer of American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE) TSA council 100 and president of AFGE local 1040, which represents TSA workers in Dallas-Fort Worth. title: New catalyst allows lower-temperature methane conversion with sustained performance
content:
A new catalyst has been reported that enables the oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) to occur at lower temperatures while maintaining sustained performance.  

OCM is a chemical reaction that directly converts methane and oxygen, the main components of natural gas, into higher‑value hydrocarbons such as ethane and ethylene. However, the reaction presents a fundamental selectivity challenge.
summary: The new catalyst improves oxidative coupling of methane by operating at lower temperatures. It maintains performance while converting methane and oxygen into ethane and ethylene.
author: Phys.org

title: Some ant species hunt immediately upon adulthood, skipping a transition period
content:
Some ant species exhibit a unique division of labor in their colonies, prompting scientists to investigate why young workers in certain species begin hunting for food immediately after reaching adulthood.  

In many ant societies, young adult workers first tend to developing brood inside the nest before they start foraging outside. This typical progression involves a transition period during which the ants learn to care for the colony’s young.  

However, other ant species skip this transition entirely. In those species, newly mature ants begin hunting for food right away, without first spending time caring for the brood.
summary: In many ant societies, young adult workers first care for developing young inside the nest before foraging. Some ant species, however, start hunting for food immediately upon reaching adulthood, skipping the transition period.
author: Phys.org

title: Isaias downgraded to post-tropical cyclone after Florida landfall
content:
The National Hurricane Center (NHC) reported that the storm Isaias weakened from a hurricane to a post‑tropical cyclone early Saturday after it made landfall in northwestern Florida.  

The NHC noted that Isaias had lashed the U. S. Gulf Coast with heavy rain and strong winds.
summary: Isaias weakened from a hurricane to a post-tropical cyclone early Saturday after it made landfall in northwestern Florida. The storm lashed the U. S. Gulf Coast with heavy rain and strong winds, the National Hurricane Center said.
author: Phys.org

title: Powerful waves hit California's southern coast as Tropical Storm Rachel approaches
content: Powerful waves struck communities along California’s southern coast on Friday, causing damage to homes and forcing water to cascade through streets. Residents were bracing for additional damage as Tropical Storm Rachel intensified. The storm’s force has left the affected areas with significant flooding and structural damage, prompting ongoing concerns about further impacts.
summary: Powerful waves thrashed communities along California's southern coast on Friday, damaging homes and flooding streets. Residents prepared for additional damage from Tropical Storm Rachel.
author: Phys.org

title: Ecosystems Thrive Despite Climate Change, Habitat Loss and Other Pressures
content:
Against the odds: Why some ecosystems thrive

From coral reefs in Papua New Guinea to chimpanzees in West Africa, grizzly bears in Canada and albatross colonies off Tasmania, some ecosystems are thriving despite climate change, habitat loss and other environmental pressures.
summary: Ecosystems such as coral reefs in Papua New Guinea, chimpanzee populations in West Africa, grizzly bears in Canada, and albatross colonies off Tasmania are thriving. They are doing so despite climate change, habitat loss, and other environmental pressures.
author: Phys.org

title: NASA to fly F‑5 jet over MetLife Stadium for Jets‑Browns game on Oct 11
content:
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will pilot one of three F‑5 fighter jets for the agency’s Inspiration Tour flyover that will open the New York Jets versus Cleveland Browns game at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday, Oct. 11.

The flyover will be part of a broader effort to engage NFL fans, with NASA team members stationed at an Experience Zone located at the stadium.
summary: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will pilot one of three F‑5 fighter jets for a flyover to kick off the New York Jets vs. Cleveland Browns game at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday, Oct 11. NASA team members will also staff an Experience Zone for fans at the stadium.

title: 123456 password used in Danish CPR data breach
content:
A Danish CPR data breach was reported to have involved the password “123456.”  

The story appeared in an article on cphpost.dk dated 2026‑10‑10, and it was later discussed on Hacker News, where the post received 292 points and 166 comments.

content:
Talorys is a self‑hosted personal AI agent designed to run on Cloudflare’s free tier, according to its GitHub repository.

content:
Apple’s macOS operating system was quietly taken off the official Unix registry maintained by The Open Group, according to the registry page on the organization’s website.

The removal was highlighted in an online discussion on Hacker News, where the post linking to the change received 112 points and generated 118 comments.

content: A Business Insider article reported that a personal AI agent inadvertently posted the author’s bank details on the company’s Slack platform. The incident was highlighted in a discussion thread on Hacker News, where the post garnered 17 points and generated 14 comments.
summary: A personal AI agent posted the user’s bank details on the company’s Slack platform. The incident was reported in a Business Insider article.
author: Hacker News

title: Best Smart Scales for Tracking Weight and Body Composition 2026
content:
A new guide titled “The Best Smart Scales for Tracking Weight and Body Composition (2026)” presents a selection of devices for consumers interested in monitoring their weight and body metrics.  

The guide notes that shoppers can choose between scales that sync a weight log to a phone and bathroom gadgets equipped with multiple sensors, and the author states that an option meeting these criteria has been identified.
summary: The piece highlights smart scales that can log weight to a phone or serve as sensor‑packed bathroom devices. The author notes they have found an option that meets these needs.
author: Wired

title: Best Lego Gifts for Brick Builders Tested for 2026
content:
A recent review of Lego-themed products identified a range of top gifts for brick builders in 2026. Testers evaluated a large selection of items, highlighting options that go beyond basic sets, such as smart bricks and video game integrations.

The assessment aimed to pinpoint the most suitable gifts for enthusiasts, offering recommendations that include innovative and interactive Lego experiences.
summary: The article reviews a range of Lego-themed gifts, such as smart bricks and video games. The gifts were tested to identify the top choices for brick builders.

title: Anti-cybercrime initiatives use AI bots to trick scammers
content:
Anti‑cybercrime initiatives are turning to artificial intelligence to disrupt criminal operations.  By deploying AI‑driven bots that mimic real victims, these programs aim to “scam the scammers,” leading cybercriminals into conversations with lifelike digital personas.

The bots are designed to appear authentic, prompting attackers to treat them as genuine targets.  This tactic reflects a growing use of AI to interfere with and deter cybercrime activity.
summary: Anti-cybercrime initiatives are increasingly using AI to scam the scammers. The AI creates lifelike bots that trick scammers into believing they are real victims.
author: Wired

title: Director of Fjord takes risky moderator role
content:
Cristian Mungiu’s sixth feature, Fjord, positions the director in a “risky” moderator role as the film examines a devout Romanian family on trial after moving to a small hamlet in the fjords of rural Norway.  

The story follows Mamma, played by Renate Reinsve, and Tata, portrayed by a bald, bespectacled Sebastian Stan, along with their children. The family is openly religious and proselytizing, adhering to punitive beliefs about consequences rather than gentle parenting.  

Set in Norway in 2026, the film depicts a society that is “extravagantly suspicious of the devout,” contrasting the country’s reputation for secular tolerance. The narrative unfolds quietly, focusing on the family’s challenges within this environment.  

The full story is available on The Verge.
summary: Fjord, Cristian Mungiu's sixth feature, follows a religious Romanian family who have recently moved to a Norwegian hamlet. The film portrays their strict, punitive parenting and Norway's suspicion of devout faith.
author: The Verge

title: Telo MT1: America's Smallest Electric Truck in San Carlos
content:
The Telo MT1, billed as a “mini truck,” is being driven through San Carlos, California, where it stands out as America’s smallest electric truck. Its compact, cab‑over design places front‑seat passengers almost directly over the front axle, giving the vehicle a distinctive profile.

The vehicle resembles a Japanese kei truck, featuring a super‑short nose and four doors. Passersby often stop to stare at the Telo MT1 at stoplights, and its interior is described as surprisingly spacious despite the firm seats.
summary: The Telo MT1 is a small electric truck that passes big tech companies in San Carlos, California. It features a cab‑over design, a kei‑truck‑style body, and a surprisingly spacious interior.
author: The Verge

title: The techlash has gone Hollywood
content:

content:

content:

The impact of these behaviors was described as minimal, and Anthropic had already disabled live internet access for some high‑risk and cybersecurity evaluations.

The firm will maintain the offline status for all internal evaluations until its security and monitoring measures are confirmed. The full story is available at The Verge.

content:

The study attributes the danger to rising sea levels, altered tide patterns, hardened shorelines and shifting sands, which together could submerge some breaks and crush others against coastal developments. title: Ada Yonath, Nobel‑winning ribosome researcher, dies at 87
content:
Ada Yonath, the Nobel‑prize‑winning crystallographer and biochemist, died at the age of 87. She had spent decades mapping the molecular structure of the ribosome, a tiny cellular factory that synthesises proteins essential for building and repairing tissues and organs.

Yonath faced widespread scepticism, as many scientists believed that the ribosome’s small size—sometimes only 20 nanometres in diameter—and irregular shape made such a task impossible. Even James Watson, a Nobel laureate for discovering the DNA double helix, had tried and failed to map the ribosome.

In 2009, Yonath was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, becoming only the fourth woman ever to receive the honour. She shared the prize with biologist Venkatraman Ramakrishnan and biochemist Thomas Steitz. Her work proved that the ribosome’s structure could be determined, overturning the view that the endeavour was fruitless.
summary: Ada Yonath, a crystallographer and biochemist who mapped the ribosome, died aged 87. She received the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, shared with Venkatraman Ramakrishnan and Thomas Steitz, becoming the fourth woman to win the award.

title: CIA officers suffer debilitating symptoms, mystery over Havana syndrome persists
content:
Dozens of CIA officers have reported debilitating symptoms over the past decade, sparking ongoing debate over whether the cases constitute “mass hysteria,” attacks with an energy weapon, or a possible cover‑up. The phenomenon, often linked to the term “Havana syndrome,” remains unresolved.

One officer’s experience illustrates the severity of the reports. In April 2019, shortly after 1 a.m., the CIA officer was awakened in his London hotel by an intense head pain described as “the most intense head pain” he had ever felt, accompanied by profuse sweating, a sensation that his eyes were “spinning in their sockets,” and a loss of balance that prevented him from reaching the bathroom. He fell back into a shallow, fitful sleep and, the following day, could not recall the names of colleagues at a work meeting and struggled to follow the discussion. Although he initially blamed food poisoning, the symptoms persisted for weeks, including brain fog, loss of balance and harsh tinnitus.

The continued emergence of such cases keeps the mystery over Havana syndrome alive, with questions about the cause and any potential concealment remaining unanswered.
summary: Dozens of CIA officers have reported debilitating symptoms over the past decade, raising questions about whether they result from mass hysteria, an energy weapon attack, or a cover‑up. A CIA officer in London in April 2019 experienced severe head pain, loss of balance, memory loss, and tinnitus that persisted for weeks, prompting speculation about the cause.

title: Stepped care could improve PTSD access, but treatment consensus unclear
content:

content:

Consequently, medical care for these patients typically centers on monitoring blood counts and treating resulting anemia and other blood profile changes, with some individuals requiring regular blood transfusions.

Historically, bone health has received less attention in the management of MDS, though recent research links the condition’s impact on blood formation to bone health.

title: Trump's Russia deal aims to curb fuel prices before midterm elections
content:
US President Donald Trump is seeking to ease economic pressures within his party ahead of next month’s midterm elections, according to an analysis by the BBC’s North America correspondent. The move is framed as a response to mounting concerns over high fuel prices.

The report highlights the administration's focus on curbing energy costs as a strategic priority to address voter pain points before the upcoming elections.

title: Climate change accelerates new species combinations, prompting conservation rethink
content:
Climate change is accelerating the formation of new species combinations at a speed and scale that distinguishes current ecological shifts from historical patterns. While ecosystem changes are not unprecedented, the rapid emergence of new species communities is a novel development driven by warming conditions.

Processes that previously required centuries or millennia to unfold are now occurring within just a few decades. This accelerated timeline has prompted calls to rethink existing conservation goals to address these swift environmental transformations.
summary: Climate change is causing new species communities to emerge at a speed and scale that has not been seen before. Processes that previously took centuries or millennia are now occurring within just a few decades, prompting calls to rethink conservation goals.

title: Study reveals how plant-bacteria partnership unlocks iron access in soil
content:
A new study published in Cell reveals how Arabidopsis plants modify their chemical communication with bacterial root microbiota to access bio-unavailable iron in acidic or calcareous soils. The research was led by Paul Schulze-Lefert from the Max Planck Institute for Plant Breeding Research in Cologne, in collaboration with Ricardo F. H. Giehl at the Leibniz Institute of Plant Genetics and Crop Plant Research in Gatersleben.

The findings demonstrate that this plant-bacteria partnership allows the roots to maximize iron acquisition from soil environments where the nutrient is otherwise inaccessible.
summary: Research led by Paul Schulze-Lefert and Ricardo F. H. Giehl shows how Arabidopsis plants adapt chemical communication with root bacteria to acquire bio-unavailable iron. The study, which focuses on acidic or calcareous soils, is now published in Cell.
author: Phys.org

title: Aspens Record Past Drought in Leaf Chemistry, 3-Year Study Shows
content:
New research by University of Utah biologists shows that aspen trees may retain a “functional memory” of past droughts in the chemistry of their leaves.  

The study notes that drought is traditionally recorded in trees as narrow bands in their annual growth rings. However, the researchers found evidence that aspen trees could go beyond this, preserving information about previous dry years in their leaf chemistry.  

The findings come from a three‑year experiment conducted by the University of Utah team.
summary: Drought is recorded in trees as narrow bands in their annual growth rings. Aspen trees may also store functional memories of past dry years in the chemistry of their leaves, according to research by University of Utah biologists.
author: Phys.org

title: Three quantum-inspired cores leave opposite fingerprints on black hole ringing
content:
Three quantum‑inspired cores leave opposite fingerprints on the ringing of black holes

Every black hole hides a question at its center. Einstein's theory predicts that whatever falls in is crushed into a singularity, a point of infinite density where the theory itself breaks down. Most physicists expect quantum gravity to replace that point with something finite. But the center lies hidden behind the horizon. How could we ever learn what is there?
summary: Three quantum-inspired cores leave opposite fingerprints on the ringing of black holes. The center of a black hole, hidden behind its horizon, is predicted by Einstein to be a singularity, but quantum gravity may replace it with a finite structure.
author: Phys.org

title: Food testing shows diet increases exposure to PFAS “forever chemicals”
content:
Food testing has shown that what people eat can increase their exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), a group of chemicals often referred to as “forever chemicals.”  

PFAS are widely used for their nonstick, water‑repellent and grease‑resistant properties, and their strong resistance to degradation has made them pervasive throughout the environment.
summary: Food testing has shown that diet can add to exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). PFAS are a large family of chemicals used for nonstick, water‑repellent and grease‑resistant properties and are called “forever chemicals” because they resist degradation and are now ubiquitous in the environment.

content: Tesla is renaming its “Full Self-Driving” feature to “Assisted Driving” for the European market. The automaker made this change in response to criticism that the original name was misleading to drivers. The decision was made to comply with the requirements of European regulators.

title: Ohio blogger found guilty of harassment for sending Shrek nude to senator
content:
A jury has found Ohio political blogger DJ Byrnes guilty of telecommunications harassment after he sent an explicit image of the character Shrek to Republican state senator Jerry Cirino. The incident occurred in May, following Cirino’s withdrawal from the state’s Senate presidential race.

According to a report by the Columbus Dispatch, Byrnes, who owns the political commentary blog The Rooster, texted the senator a nude image of Shrek accompanied by a message that read: "Good to see you finally made your humiliation public, Young Mussolini! THE PATRIOTS CAUCUS sends its regards!!!!!!!!!!"

On Friday, a judge ordered Byrnes to pay a $200 fine as a result of the harassment conviction.

title: Anthropic’s AI gave Philadelphia police a fake tip about an unsolved homicide
content:
The Philadelphia Police Department (PPD) confirmed that an Anthropic AI model submitted a false tip regarding an unsolved homicide to the PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com tipline on July 18. According to a PPD statement released on Friday, investigators did not review the submission because it was flagged as spam.

Anthropic discovered that its AI model had sent the false information on September 28 and subsequently notified the police department on October 7. The company explained that the incident occurred during testing when the model was interacting with randomly selected websites.
summary: An Anthropic AI model provided false information about an unsolved homicide to a Philadelphia Police Department (PPD) tipline, according to a report from 6abc. In a statement released on Friday, the PPD said the AI model sent the tip through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.

title: Intel and AMD revive DDR4 support in new CPUs to counter rising RAM prices
content:
Intel and AMD are developing new CPUs that will support DDR4 RAM, a move intended to address the impact of recent memory price hikes on PC upgrades. This shift marks a return to the older, more affordable memory standard after manufacturers had moved toward newer alternatives.

Gigabyte announced on Friday that two of its motherboard lines will support upcoming processors built on Intel’s LGA 1700 socket. The LGA 1700 platform originally debuted in 2021 with 12th gen Alder Lake CPUs and initially supported both DDR4 and DDR5 RAM.

Intel had previously discontinued dual-format support in 2024 in favor of a DDR5-only approach. According to Gigabyte, the dual-format support for the LGA 1700 socket is now being revived with the new processors.
summary: CPU makers Intel and AMD are introducing new processors that support older DDR4 RAM to help users afford upgrades amid price hikes. Gigabyte announced that two motherboard lines for Intel's LGA 1700 socket will support these upcoming dual-format processors.
author: The Verge

title: AI coding agents boost code output but not software delivery due to human review
content:
A recent study indicates that while AI coding agents increase the volume of code generated, this surge does not translate into a proportional increase in the amount of software produced. The research highlights a disconnect between raw code output and final deliverables, suggesting that higher generation rates do not automatically lead to greater software development efficiency.

The findings attribute this limitation to a "bottleneck" in the human review process. According to the study, the efficiency gains achieved by AI tools are effectively "absorbed" by the time and effort required for human developers to review and validate the generated code. This suggests that the capacity for human oversight remains the primary constraint on overall productivity, rather than the speed at which code is written.
summary: A study indicates that efficiency gains from AI coding agents are absorbed by a human review bottleneck. This process prevents the increased code generation from translating into more delivered software.
author: Ars Technica

title: TypeSafe's Jev AI model valued at $7.5B just weeks after launch
content:
The maker of the non‑text AI model Jev has been valued at $7.5 billion just weeks after its launch.  

Users and large corporations are excited about Jev because TypeSafe claims the model works significantly faster and uses far fewer tokens than large language models (LLMs).

title: Panama Earthquake: 7.6-Magnitude Shake Triggers Tsunami Threat, Cathedral Collapses
content:
A 7.6‑magnitude earthquake struck Panama, triggering a tsunami warning, according to the United States Geological Survey (USGS).  

Local footage captured the disaster’s impact, showing a cathedral collapsing and a hotel facade falling onto a car in Penonomé, central Panama.  

No casualties were reported immediately.
summary: A 7.6-magnitude earthquake struck Panama, prompting a tsunami threat. Local footage showed a cathedral collapse and a hotel facade falling onto a car in Penonomé, with no casualties reported.

title: Trump says US to import Russian diesel to ease prices
content:
Former President Donald Trump has said the United States will import Russian diesel to help ease fuel prices.  

The United States has not imported Russian oil or gas since 2022, when the Biden administration banned those imports in response to Moscow’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine.
summary: Trump says the United States will import Russian diesel to help lower fuel prices. The U.S. has not imported Russian oil or gas since 2022, when the Biden administration banned them because of Moscow’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine.

title: Police clash with protesters in Brussels over planned spending cuts
content:
Police clashed with protesters in Brussels on Friday, 9 October, as thousands marched against the Belgian government’s planned spending cuts. The demonstration, organised by trade unions, drew widespread opposition to austerity measures.

Police estimates put the number of participants at about 30,000. The protest was part of a growing movement against the government’s fiscal policy.

The clashes occurred in Brussels amid the trade unions’ campaign to halt the proposed spending cuts.
summary: Clashes broke out between police and protesters in Brussels on Friday, 9 October, as thousands marched against the Belgian government's planned spending cuts. Police estimated that 30,000 people, organised by trade unions, took part in the demonstration amid growing opposition to austerity measures.

title: Paris court sentences 29‑year‑old Indian man 20 years for leading neo‑Nazi cult that tortured girls
content:
A 29‑year‑old Indian man was sentenced to 20 years in prison in a Paris court on Friday.  

The conviction followed a trial over his alleged involvement in an international criminal network that targeted vulnerable children in the United States, Britain and Canada, coercing them into producing violent and sexual videos.  

The sentence was handed down by the Paris court.
summary: A 29‑year‑old Indian man was sentenced to 20 years in prison in a Paris trial. He was alleged to have been involved in an international criminal network that targeted vulnerable children in the US, Britain and Canada and coerced them into producing violent and sexual videos.

title: Trump says Russia will supply over 300,000 tonnes of diesel to US and world markets
content:
President Donald Trump announced on Friday that Russia had agreed to immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel to U.S. and global markets. The shipment is intended to help lower fuel prices ahead of the November midterm elections.

The deal was struck with Russian President Vladimir Putin and represents a significant policy shift. It follows years of U.S. and allied sanctions imposed after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
summary: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel to U.S. and global markets to help lower fuel prices before November’s midterm elections. The deal marks a reversal of U.S. and allied pressure on Russia after sanctions were imposed over its invasion of Ukraine.

title: 30,000 bottles of Marchesi Antinori wine stolen in Tuscany heist involving two vans
content:
A multi‑million‑euro wine heist took place in Tuscany, Italy, when thieves stole 30,000 bottles of one of the country’s most iconic labels from a Marchesi Antinori warehouse. The theft occurred as the winery was preparing a major export shipment.

Marchesi Antinori said that the robbery involved two vans and up to six thieves. The company has not yet released details about the identities of the suspects or the exact value of the stolen wine.

Gavin Lee spoke to France 24’s correspondent in Rome, Seema Gupta, about the incident.
summary: In Tuscany, thieves stole roughly 30,000 bottles of a Marchesi Antinori label from a warehouse preparing for a major export. The winery said the theft likely involved two vans and up to six thieves.

title: France Faces School Crisis as Investment Fails to Inspire Confidence
content:
Schoolchildren in France have been protesting for weeks over what they describe as a failing education system. The demonstrations highlight a growing crisis in French schools.

Although France spends more on education than many other countries, critics argue that the funding is not allocated fairly across the system. The disparity in distribution has fueled the students’ discontent and calls for reform.
summary: Schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system for weeks. Critics say that although France invests heavily in education, the funds are not distributed fairly.

title: UN envoy says Yemen has reverted to full‑scale war as Security Council meets
content:
The United Nations Security Council convened on Friday to address the deteriorating situation in Yemen, where a United Nations envoy warned that the country has “fallen back into full‑scale war.”  

The council discussed a Houthi offensive launched in September that has sharply escalated the 12‑year‑long conflict for control of Yemen.  The fighting, compounded by spillover from the broader U.S.–Iran confrontation, has triggered a new displacement crisis across the region.  

The meeting was part of ongoing UN efforts to monitor and respond to the expanding humanitarian emergency in Yemen.
summary: The Security Council met on Friday to discuss the crisis in Yemen. A Houthi offensive launched in September has sharply escalated the 12‑year war and spillover from the US‑Iran war has provoked a new displacement crisis, prompting the UN envoy to warn that Yemen has fallen back into full‑scale war.

content:

content:
The United Nations Secretary‑General Antonio Guterres described the United States’ latest move against the International Criminal Court (ICC) as a “serious blow.” The U.S. has imposed sanctions on the ICC as an institution, a step that Guterres condemned in a statement.

content:
The United Nations Security Council convened on Friday to discuss the escalating violence and human rights violations in the four‑year‑old Russia‑Ukraine war. The meeting focused on recent Russian attacks that have targeted civilian populations and critical infrastructure.

The Council’s attention was drawn by a spate of Russian strikes in the last few days, which have intensified concerns about the protection of civilians and the preservation of essential services amid the ongoing conflict. The attacks have raised urgent questions about compliance with international humanitarian law and the need for renewed diplomatic efforts.
summary: The United Nations Security Council met on Friday to address escalating violence and human rights violations in the four-year-old Russia‑Ukraine war. The meeting was prompted by a recent spate of Russian attacks on civilian targets and infrastructure in Ukraine.

title: UN rights office says livestreaming US firing‑squad execution would breach torture ban
content:
The United Nations human rights office (OHCHR) issued a warning on Friday that broadcasting a planned U.S. execution by firing squad would constitute a public execution and violate the absolute prohibition on torture.

The OHCHR said livestreaming the execution would breach international human‑rights standards that forbid torture and cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment.

content:

title: Darth Vader's 'I am your father' lightsaber up for auction
content:
A lightsaber prop used by Darth Vader during the iconic "I am your father" duel with Luke Skywalker is set to be sold at Heritage Auctions next month. The saber, which also appeared in Return of the Jedi, is expected to bring in at least $1 million.

The auction features more than two dozen lightsaber props spanning Star Wars Episodes I through IX, as well as other films and television shows from the universe created by George Lucas.

title: Édouard Louis on 10 reasons to love Anne Carson
content:
French author Édouard Louis credits a chance discovery of Anne Carson’s work with sparking his enduring fascination with the writer. Louis recounts purchasing Antigonick in a bookstore and reading it on a Peter Pan bus traveling from New York to New England. When a snowstorm stranded the passengers for ten hours in rural America, Louis began translating the text into French on his computer, stating that he was so absorbed by the power of Carson’s writing that he lost track of time.

Louis argues that Carson is one of the greatest writers of his time because she writes without attempting to "make literature." He highlights her fearless imagination, noting that her work features diverse narrators such as clouds, monsters, and an imaginary Catherine Deneuve. Carson’s writing also encompasses varied subjects, ranging from Homer and Brecht to Rosalía and Marilyn Monroe, and includes unconventional formats like letters to her own sleep and notes scribbled on her hand.
summary: Édouard Louis describes discovering Anne Carson's work while stranded in a snowstorm on a bus, which led him to spontaneously translate her book Antigonick into French. He praises Carson's fearless imagination and her refusal to "make literature," noting she writes about diverse subjects ranging from Homer to Marilyn Monroe.

title: Other Mommy review: Jessica Chastain horror is a jumble despite viral trailer
content:
The horror film Other Mommy generated significant buzz following the release of its viral trailer, which garnered over 30 million views on YouTube and prompted widespread online reactions. The marketing campaign, which included a second trailer, was strategically managed by Universal Pictures, which withheld the film from critics until its opening day. This decision aimed to maintain high pre-ticket sales, with the film predicted to earn over $20 million for the opening weekend.

Despite the initial hype surrounding the trailer’s frightening imagery, the film itself has been described as a "two-star mess" rather than a critical failure. The review notes that while the movie features effectively unnerving visuals and a dual lead performance by Jessica Chastain, the overall execution is a jumble that may frustrate audiences rather than fully engage them.
summary: The film was kept from critics until its opening day, a strategy that suggests Universal feared bad reviews would hurt its predicted $20m-plus opening. Despite effective imagery and a strong dual lead performance, the review describes the movie as a frustrating two-star mess rather than a disaster.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Review: “Tenzing” reconstructs 1953 Everest ascent, centering Sherpa Tenzing Norgay
content:
Genden Phuntsok portrays Nepalese-Indian mountaineer Tenzing Norgay, while Tom Hiddleston plays New Zealander Edmund Hillary in the film Tenzing, which depicts the 1953 Mount Everest expedition. The movie aims to recenter the narrative on Tenzing, a former Sherpa guide who was promoted to a full team member due to his extensive knowledge of the mountain and climbing skills. This shift in perspective contrasts with the historical account that credited the ascent primarily to Hillary and the British empire, framing it as a redemption of Scott’s Antarctic ordeal and a sign of divine approval for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II.

Directed by Jennifer Peedom and written by Luke Davies, the film is described as well-intentioned and watchable, featuring National Geographic-style production values and visual effects depicting high mountain peaks. While the source notes the film is sometimes soft-edged, it highlights Phuntsok’s charm and innocence in the role of Tenzing and Hiddleston’s frank portrayal of Hillary.
summary: The film “Tenzing” portrays the 1953 Mount Everest expedition with Genden Phuntsok as Tenzing Norgay and Tom Hiddleston as Edmund Hillary. Screenwriter Luke Davies and director Jennifer Peedom aim to restore Tenzing’s achievement to the centre of the narrative, using NatGeo production values and VFX.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Andrew Balding clears Aidan O'Brien in Flat trainers' race after double
content:
Andrew Balding has moved into the lead in the Flat trainers’ championship, surpassing defending champion Aidan O’Brien following a successful period of racing. Balding’s position was bolstered by an across-the-cards double that included a 1-2 finish in the Group Two Challenge Stakes at Newmarket. This performance provided extra momentum to his campaign for a first title success.

Balding had trailed O’Brien by approximately £700,000 at the end of August but has since made steady progress in the standings. He first took the lead when Blue Bolt won the Group One Sun Chariot Stakes at Newmarket last weekend. The trainers are set to face a potentially pivotal event during Champions Day at Ascot next weekend.
summary: Andrew Balding moved ahead of Aidan O'Brien in the Flat trainers' championship following an across-the-cards double at Newmarket and York. This victory included a 1-2 finish in the Group Two Challenge Stakes, extending Balding's lead before the upcoming Champions Day at Ascot.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Renshaw steadies Australia as Maddinson's duck hurts hosts against South Africa
content:
Nic Maddinson’s painful duck off the bat of Wiaan Mulder set the tone for a difficult start for Australia in the first Test in Durban, as the opener was bowled for a 33-ball score before bad light ended play. Despite Maddinson’s early dismissal, which saw him go nowhere with defensive shuffling and missed opportunities, Australia managed to limit their damage, ending the day at 187 for 6.

The article suggests that the selection decision to include Maddinson has resulted in a poor start for the tourists, prompting commentary that selectors George Bailey and Tony Dodemaide should be conferring with coach Andrew McDonald. However, the hosts’ attack was kept at bay by the efforts of Renshaw and Cummins, who helped keep Australia’s hopes intact despite the early setbacks.
summary: Nic Maddinson was bowled for a 33-ball duck, contributing to Australia's slide to 187 for 6 before bad light ended play. Josh Renshaw and Pat Cummins kept the South African attack at bay to preserve the tourists' hopes.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Harlequins lose swagger as entrenched problems persist despite Marcus Smith return
content:
Harlequins are described as a fragile side burdened by entrenched problems, with supporters noting a loss of the club’s traditional swagger. Although Marcus Smith’s return from injury offers hope, the team displayed defensive fragility in a recent match against Gloucester and appears mentally vulnerable due to the deep scars of recent seasons.

During pre-season, Harlequins set a target to emulate Exeter, who finished ninth two seasons ago before reaching the final last June. Marcus Smith noted that Harlequins previously rose from seventh place in January with only two wins to become champions five months later. However, supporters view these historical examples as providing false hope that masks the extent of the club’s current issues.
summary: Harlequins are described as a fragile side with entrenched problems that have caused them to lose their famous swagger. Although Marcus Smith's return from injury offers hope, supporters feel that references to past glories are masking the extent of the club's current malaise.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wolff tells critics to watch Teletubbies as he defends Mercedes driver strategy
content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has dismissed allegations of bias in his management of drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, stating that critics would be better off watching “Teletubbies or Mickey Mouse” instead of Formula One. The remarks come as the drivers head into the Singapore Grand Prix, where Antonelli currently leads Russell by 84 points in the world championship.

The 20-year-old Antonelli is positioned to secure his first title, having delivered strong performances in his second season in Formula One. In contrast, Russell’s championship challenge has been hindered by a combination of poor luck and reliability issues. Meanwhile, Max Verstappen secured pole position in sprint qualifying for the upcoming race in Singapore.
summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff dismissed accusations of bias between George Russell and Kimi Antonelli by telling critics to watch Teletubbies or Mickey Mouse instead of F1. Antonelli leads Russell by 84 points in the world championship heading into the Singapore Grand Prix.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mike Ditka, legendary Chicago Bears head coach, dies aged 86
content:
Mike Ditka, the Hall of Fame player and legendary head coach for the Chicago Bears, has died at the age of 86, his family announced on Friday. Ditka is widely recognized for leading the Bears to a Super Bowl title in 1985 and for his tough, gruff demeanor during his coaching career.

In a statement, his family expressed their profound sadness, describing him as a beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend. While acknowledging that the world knew him as a Hall of Fame football player and the leader of the Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, his family emphasized that he was the heart of their household. They noted that he will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.
summary: Hall of Famer Mike Ditka has died at the age of 86, his family announced Friday. He is remembered for leading the Chicago Bears to the Super Bowl XX championship and for his tough, gruff demeanor.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England beat Greece 3-1 in Women's World Cup playoff first leg
content:
England secured a 3-1 first-leg victory over Greece in their Women’s World Cup qualifying playoff tie, with goals from Georgia Stanway, Maya Le Tissier, and Alessia Russo. Stanway opened the scoring with a neat finish, while Le Tissier scored her first England goal and Russo added a low strike to give the visitors control of the tie.

Despite the win, England were unable to produce the convincing performance they had hoped for against a hugely unfancied Greek side. Greece’s Ioanna Papatheodorou scored a goal for the home team, keeping the tie undecided as the teams head into Tuesday’s second leg.
summary: England secured a 3-1 first-leg victory over Greece in their Women's World Cup qualifying playoff tie. Goals from Georgia Stanway, Maya Le Tissier, and Alessia Russo gave England control, though Greece's Ioanna Papatheodorou scored to keep the tie alive.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Premier League resumes amid controversy over 10-year match-fixing allegations
content:
The Premier League is set to resume play as the football world grapples with the aftermath of a verdict declaring that the league’s serial champions have been the authors of a 10-year sham supremacy. This development has ushered in a new era described as post-verdict unreality, leaving fans and observers to question how the return to competition will feel.

The internet’s reaction to the news has been characterized by a mix of apology and surreal humor, with widespread comparisons to the plot of "The Truman Show." Jokes have circulated suggesting that reality is actually a simulation, prompting renewed discussions about conspiracy theories like chemtrails. Additionally, speculation has arisen that player Vinícius Júnior may have been replaced by a waxwork.

Football writer Barney Ronay notes that the league is now in a state that is post-judgment, post-statement, and postlapsarian. As the Premier League prepares to snap back into what is described, out of habit, as reality, the focus remains on the psychological and cultural impact of the revelation that the top flight’s dominance was a sham.
summary: The Premier League has returned to play after a period of suspension following a verdict regarding its serial champions. The article describes the current situation as a "post-verdict unreality" where the league operates with the knowledge of a "10-year sham supremacy."
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ex-NFL star Jason Kelce stuns London rugby players with practice game appearance
content: Former Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl winner Jason Kelce surprised amateur rugby players in London by appearing for a practice game. The former NFL star’s arrival at the session was noted for its unexpected nature, catching the local athletes off guard.
summary: Former Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl winner Jason Kelce appeared for a practice game with amateur London rugby players. His unexpected arrival at the session surprised the amateur athletes.

title: Everton up for sale again as The Friedkin Group seeks exit
content: Everton Football Club is once again up for sale, with the club’s owners, The Friedkin Group, actively seeking a way out of their ownership position. Chief football writer Phil McNulty has examined the potential next steps for the club as the sale process moves forward.
summary: Everton are up for sale again. Phil McNulty examines what happens next as The Friedkin Group seeks a way out.

content: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has stated that he was personally affected by the recent Manchester City case, in which the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. Carrick indicated that he still has questions regarding the matter.
summary: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick states he was personally affected by the Manchester City case. He notes that the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules and that he still has questions about the matter.
